judgments.catchwords: Administrative Law – Judicial review – Duty of candour – Public authority – Duty to make full and fair disclosure of all material facts – Failure to disclose that Valuation List being amended had expired – Breach of duty of candour – Consequences. Local Government Law – Valuation List – Statutory lifespan – Section 137 Local Government Act 1976 – New Valuation List must be prepared once every five years – Valuation List expires after five years – No local authority may use Valuation List for indeterminable period. Local Government Law – Valuation List – Amendment – Section 144 Local Government Act 1976 – Amendment can only be made to current Valuation List – Not to expired or outdated Valuation List – Amendment to expired list is ultra vires and void. Local Government Law – Valuation List – Section 137(2) – Saving provision – Valuation List remains in force until superseded by new list – Not a power to extend lifespan of existing list – Only temporary measure while new list being prepared– Extension of time – Section 137(3) – State Authority may extend period for preparation of new Valuation List – Not power to extend validity of existing Valuation List – No extension granted in present case. Local Government Law – Retrospective rates – Amendment to current Valuation List may have retrospective effect – But no retrospective effect where Valuation List itself has expired – Question of retrospectivity becomes academic.

judgments.title: AMIRHAMZAH BIN KARIM v Mahani Catherine Binti Hijjas & ors
judgments.catchwords: This representative action under s 9(c) of the Societies Act 1966 concerned the alleged misappropriation of RM6 million belonging to Dewan Perniagaan Melayu Malaysia (DPMM) — a RM5 million PMO grant and RM1 million from Redberry Sdn Bhd — channelled into a related foundation's account rather than DPMM Pusat's MED-approved account. The High Court held that DPMM Pusat, DPMM Pulau Pinang, and the Foundation are separate legal entities, so the transfer breached Article 29.3 of DPMM's Constitution. The funds were found to be diverted without MED approval and misapplied on a single politically-tinged Langkawi programme, rejecting the defences of mandate, blanket approval, and private arrangement as abandoned, contradicted by contemporaneous evidence, or departures from the pleadings. Breaches of fiduciary duty were established, but claims of personal misappropriation, conspiracy to injure, and exemplary damages were dismissed. The defendants were held liable as constructive trustees, with an order for account and inquiry, tracing, and general damages. Societies Act 1966; representative action; breach of fiduciary duty; constructive trust; misapplication of funds; personal misappropriation; separate legal personality; conflict of interest; departure from pleadings; conspiracy by unlawful means; adverse inference; account and inquiry; tracing.

judgments.title: BADAN PENGURUSAN BERSAMA BOTANIKA v BAYOU BAY DEVELOPMENT SDN BHD
judgments.catchwords: Sivil – Permohonan membatalkan pliding – Aturan 18 Kaedah 19(1)(a), (b) dan (d) Kaedah-Kaedah Mahkamah 2012 – Kuasa luar biasa Mahkamah – Ujian “plainly and obviously unsustainable” – Tuntutan yang remeh, menyusahkan dan penyalahgunaan proses Mahkamah. Strata – Badan Pengurusan Bersama (JMB) – Akta Pengurusan Strata 2013 s 143(2) – Skop kuasa dan fungsi JMB – Pengurusan dan penyenggaraan harta bersama (common property) – Sama ada JMB mempunyai locus standi untuk mendakwa pemaju berasaskan perjanjian jual beli individu dan representasi pra-kontrak – JMB mempunyai personaliti undang-undang tetapi tiada hak substantif dalam SPA antara pemaju dan pembeli individu. Kontrak – Privity of contract – Perjanjian jual beli (SPA) antara pemaju dan pembeli individu – Hak kontraktual hanya pada pihak-pihak SPA – JMB bukan pihak kontrak – Dakwaan salah nyata dan pelanggaran kontrak terhadap pemaju berhubung urus niaga jualan unit – Sama ada “injury to the body corporate” atau “injury to the purchasers personally”. Misrepresentation – Brosur, risalah dan laman sesawang projek perumahan – Kenyataan promosi dan bahasa pemasaran – “Mere puff” dan “invitation to treat” – Sama ada boleh membentuk kausa tindakan misrepresentation / fraudulent misrepresentation / negligent misstatement – Elemen tort: duty of care, reliance, damage – Tiada reliance oleh JMB yang belum wujud ketika representasi dibuat – Representasi kepada pembeli individu, bukan kepada JMB.Striking out – Pleading Plaintif berasaskan salah nyata dan pelanggaran SPA – Tuntutan bagi pihak pembeli individu melalui JMB – Ketiadaan kausa tindakan yang munasabah – Tuntutan tidak bersumber daripada hak JMB di bawah Akta Pengurusan Strata 2013 – Perenggan 4, 27–33 dan 39.2 tidak mendedahkan kausa tindakan yang sah – Sesuai dibatalkan di bawah A.18 r.19(1)(a) dan (b) KKM 2012. Penyalahgunaan proses – JMB cuba mengitar semula pertikaian individu pembeli terhadap pemaju melalui tindakan korporat – Tuntutan tanpa hak undang-undang yang jelas (legal interest) – Usaha memanjangkan tanggungan pemaju melebihi tempoh dan skop yang dipersetujui dalam SPA – Abuse of process di bawah A.18 r.19(1)(d) KKM 2012. Remedi – Permohonan Defendan dibenarkan – Perenggan 4, 27–33 dan 39.2 Pernyataan Tuntutan Terpinda dibatalkan – Tuntutan Plaintif setakat bahagian tersebut diketepikan – Kos RM5,000 kepada Defendan.
